data.name: Beckman
data.long_meaning: The name Beckman is derived from the Old German name Beck, which means 'beck' or 'beak'. The surname Beckman is an occupational name for someone who lived by a beck or a small stream. In the Christian context, the name Beckman can be associated with the biblical character Becket, who was a saint and archbishop of Canterbury in England. The name Beckman can also symbolize courage and leadership.

Historically, this name may have been common in regions with many waterways, such as Europe. As people migrated and settled in new areas, the name Beckman spread to various parts of the world, including North America.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Christian tradition, the name Beckman can be linked to St. Thomas Becket, who was a saint and archbishop of Canterbury in England from 1162 to 1170. St. Thomas Becket is best known for refusing to endorse King Henry II's proposed legislation that would limit the power of the Church. He was eventually murdered in his cathedral by four of the king's knights. This courageous stance made St. Thomas Becket a symbol of resistance to tyranny and martyrdom. The name Beckman can therefore be seen as representing bravery, leadership, and a commitment to upholding religious principles.
